articles.title: Iran accuses UN of whitewashing US, Israeli actions
articles.summary:
Iran accuses UN of whitewashing US, Israeli actions

The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson has slammed the United Nations' human rights mechanism on Iran, accusing it of attempting to "whitewash" US and Israeli actions. 

"Exploiting the so-called Special Rapporteurship on the Situation of Human Rights in Iran to blame Iran for the crimes committed by the US and Israel amounts to nothing less than a deliberate attempt to whitewash aggression, atrocities, and unilateral coercive measures", Esmaeil Baqaei said in a post on X. 

"Such an approach is deeply misleading and profoundly disingenous," he added. 

Regardless of the politically motivated nature of the mandate imposed on the Human Rights Council by the UK، exploiting the so-called Special Rapporteurship on the Situation of Human Rights in Iran to blame Iran for the crimes committed by the US and Israel amounts to nothing less than a deliberate attempt to whitewash aggression, atrocities, and unilateral coercive measures. Such an approach is deeply misleading and profoundly disingenous.

— Esmaeil Baqaei (@IRIMFA_SPOX) October 29, 2026

articles.title: Palestinians call out ‘engineered famine’ in Gaza
articles.summary:
Palestinians call out ‘engineered famine’ in Gaza

Palestinians in Gaza accused Israeli occupation forces and traders of creating an "engineered famine" across the strip by only letting in and selling unhealthy products and junk food such as snacks and fizzy drinks, at the expense of the population’s health.

"The Israeli army allows in chocolates and cola, but won't let through fresh vegetables, chicken, or flour. They’re running a starvation policy, exactly like the first famine, so that we turn on each other and kill one another," says one resident.

According to the World Food Programme, the majority of Gaza’s population is suffering from acute food insecurity, a crisis that risks worsening with the announcement of aid cuts due to funding shortages.

articles.title: More on tanker set ablaze in Hormuz Strait
articles.summary:
More on tanker set ablaze in Hormuz Strait

A tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by a small boat with two explosive devices attached to its hull, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said in an update on Friday.

This caused blasts and sparked a fire in the vessel's engine room that temporarily disabled it. 

According to UKMTO, the crew were safe, there was no environmental impact and the fire had been extinguished. The vessel is now continuing to its next port of call.

There was no immediate answer as to who was behind the attack. 

Earlier, we reported that the tanker, transiting outbound in the Strait of Hormuz, was on fire. The incident occurred 25 nautical miles north east of Oman's Khasab.

Can Netanyahu cling onto power (again)?
articles.summary:
Can Netanyahu cling onto power (again)?

Israel's election has ended in deadlock.

Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has 53 seats, his rival Gadi Eisenkot's 48, and neither has the 61 needed to govern.

The surprise of the night: Palestinian citizens of Israel turned out in record numbers, pushing Arab parties to a record 19 seats. They did so despite armed right-wing observers in their towns and a campaign of fear from the prime minister.

Now Netanyahu's Likud claims the election was "stolen" by Arab parties. Police say there is no evidence.

Arab parties offer to back an anti-Netanyahu government, but the Zionist opposition is wary of relying on them. So who will govern Israel, and could deadlock keep Netanyahu in power anyway?

Middle East Eye Live’s Mathilda Mallinson and James Schneider speak to Joint List MK Ofer Cassif, MEE's Lubna Masarwa, and former Israeli negotiator Daniel Levy.
